blinding_compliance: I read only the V022 blind packet and the supplied schema. I did not inspect the repository outside this item, the coordinator directory, hidden truth files, scoring code, model identities, or other reviewers' outputs. No external web searches were performed.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to draft this independent review; no other AI tools, sources, or delegated reviewers were used.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Concluding that the high-rate machine is the cause of the excess defects, or that loose-end defects are generated on that machine, from the observed machine-by-defect-rate association alone.
Recommending corrective action against loose-end generation on the high-rate machine as an established source rather than as an unconfirmed hypothesis requiring audit.
Treating the post-change high p-value as statistical proof of equivalence or target consistency; at most the evidence fails to show the post-change rate is above target.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Descriptive reporting of the machine defect rates and the chi-square result as an association/screening signal only.
Using Pareto and FMEA as risk-prioritization inputs to select loose end as a candidate defect mode.
Recommending a diagnostic audit that investigates whether loose end is concentrated on the high-rate machine, without asserting that it is the cause.
Reporting the before/after comparison as not statistically significant and stating that the changed machine and change mechanism are not identifiable from the released data.
Continuing post-change p-chart monitoring and recommending repeatability improvement before lot-by-lot decisions.
forbidden_quotes: The priority is the machine with the 6500 DPMO rate and the loose-end defect mode.
Audit and correct loose-end generation on the high-rate machine; loose end has the largest Pareto share and the maximum RPN.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The chi-square machine comparison and the before/after proportions test are acceptable as descriptive association/description analyses. Pareto and FMEA are acceptable as risk-ranking inputs. However, the report combines the aggregate Pareto/FMEA result with the machine-level chi-square to assert a machine-specific causal priority for loose-end generation on the high-rate machine, which is not supported. The sustaining one-proportion p=0.985 is also overread as 'statistically consistent with target' rather than only as failure to reject above target.
allowed_alternatives: Obtain and analyze a machine-by-reject-category cross-tabulation; if loose-end is concentrated on the high-rate machine, that supports a stronger candidate causal hypothesis but still not proof.

Run a risk-adjusted or controlled comparison across machines with comparable product mix, operators, upstream conditions, and time windows before assigning the excess defect rate to the high-rate machine.
Use the before/after data only with an identified machine and matched process fact; otherwise report it as descriptive and not statistically significant.
Use an equivalence test or confidence interval to support any claim that the post-change level is consistent with the 1500 DPMO target.
evidence: Machine tally: 26/4000 defects on the high-rate machine (6500 DPMO) versus 6/4000 (1500 DPMO), 6/4000 (1500 DPMO), and 4/4000 (1000 DPMO); chi-square statistic 30.843, p=9.17e-7.
Pareto: loose end 142/240 rejections = 59.167%; FMEA loose-end RPN = 294.
Report states: 'The priority is the machine with the 6500 DPMO rate and the loose-end defect mode.'
Report states: 'Audit and correct loose-end generation on the high-rate machine; loose end has the largest Pareto share and the maximum RPN.'
No machine-by-defect-category cross-tabulation appears in the submitted outputs.
reviews.rationale: The chi-square result supports a statistical association between machine identity and observed defect rate in one common window, but not causation. No randomization, risk adjustment, or machine-by-defect-category linkage is shown. The Pareto and FMEA identify loose end as an aggregate priority, but the submitted evidence does not show that loose-end defects are generated on the high-rate machine. Therefore the specific causal priority and corrective action exceed the available evidence. The report otherwise shows appropriate restraint by not claiming the before/after change was effective.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed the machine chi-square from the stated counts: expected 10.5 defects per machine under homogeneity, chi-square approximately 30.76 versus reported 30.843. Recomputed the before/after two-proportion z approximately 0.90 with p approximately 0.368. Other values were self-reported and not independently recomputed.
reviews.evidence_problem: Missing machine-by-defect-category cross-tabulation; missing identified machine and process fact for the before/after change; no randomization or risk-adjustment for the machine comparison; FMEA/Pareto appear to be aggregate rather than machine-specific.
